content: Every gate in scripts/checks/ ships as a TRIO: the check, a committed regression suite of paired arms (for each must-flag a near-identical must-stay-quiet), and a mutation pass proving the suite discriminates. Established 2026-08-18 across four gates (shell-guards, collection-conformance, step-up-acr, plus the verify-package build-mode arms). The mutation pass is not ceremony -- it caught three suites that passed for the wrong reason: a near-miss arm whose fixture was ALSO failing for a missing prompt, a comment-stripping arm whose prose matched no control pattern, and two span arms whose fixture parens happened to be balanced so a naive counter got them right by luck. Each was rewritten so a broken check changes the VERDICT, not just the internals. Where a branch genuinely cannot be discriminated through the public interface, say so in the suite (the collection linter's paren-depth branch and two restoration-effect mutants are labelled equivalent-or-defensive) rather than leaving an arm that implies coverage it does not have. Every gate also carries a waiver with a MANDATORY reason and an unused-waiver error: a gate with no escape hatch gets weakened globally the first time an exception is legitimate, and a waiver that cannot rot stays honest.

name: A backlog item's own estimate and premise are the least reliable part of it -- re-measure before building
description: MEASURED across all eight ENGINEERING-BACKLOG items, 2026-08-18: five were wrong in a way that changed the work, and every error was cheap to find and expensive to inherit. (1) Item 1's premise -- PIT automates the manual mutation discipline -- is false; reproducing the motivating defect against the tool refuted it. (2) Item 1's 'a Gradle plugin + a threshold' does not run on Gradle 9 at all. (3) Item 2's 'about six sites' was 50, and its rule needed three exclusions no one had thought of. (4) Item 5's two-line diff names a CSS token that does not exist in the stylesheet, which would have shipped a transparent sticky header. (5) Item 6's fetch counts were taken with React StrictMode active, which double-invokes effects in dev and doubles EVERY number -- one of its three reported duplicates was not real, and one real duplicate had a different cause than the note stated. THE HABIT: before building, reproduce the item's own evidence. For a defect claim, re-create the defect and check the proposed tool catches it. For a count, re-take it in an environment you control. For a proposed diff, verify every identifier it names actually exists. Items 3 and 7 also both claimed something was missing that was already there -- a prototype (it was throwaway, genuinely gone) and a doc section (it existed and was correct), which is the standing grep-before-writing trap in backlog form.
